subscription_behavior: Two layers. (1) BLE layer, done at connect time, not by this page: BluetoothModel::onCharacteristicChanged @0xaca7c4 (called from initGattServices @0xaca690 once FFE2 was found in field_27) calls setNotifyValue(FFE2) @0xaca818 and listens to characteristic.lastValueStream() @0xaca850 with closure @0xacb7f8, which filters with an unresolved bool getter @0xacb830 and pushes every List<int> into BluetoothModel.field_43, a _BroadcastStreamController (BroadcastStreamController.add @0xacb870). (2) Page layer: _RainbowTestState::subscribeCharacteristic @0xacf8fc wraps field_43 in a _BroadcastStream @0xacf974 and listens @0xacf9a4 with closure @0xacf9dc, storing the StreamSubscription in state field_1b. No subscription is repeated per frame; the subscription is attached AFTER the D2-enable write is issued, so the very first frames (including the device's D2 echo) are delivered to a listener that already exists.
timing: No sleep between the D2-enable write and the listener attach: the callback @0xacf874 calls testModeSwitch(true) without awaiting it (no AwaitStub at 0xacf8cc) and then immediately calls subscribeCharacteristic() @0xacf8dc. Inside testModeSwitch the write is awaited (AwaitStub @0xabb028). The callback itself is not triggered by a fixed delay in this page: it is registered into a global callback list in initState and invoked later with a Duration argument (event-driven). The one concrete delay found in this code path belongs to the parent ARMOR-X Pro page, not to D2: _ArmorXProWidgetState::initState @0xab8dec registers closure 0xab8fb4 which calls subscribeCharacteristic then Future.delayed(Duration 500000 microseconds = 500 ms) @0xab8ff0-0xab9020 before getDeviceUUID; it also starts Timer.periodic @0xab8f2c whose callback @0xab8f6c only calls getBatteryParam. No re-send of D2 and no periodic D2 was found.

Masks are built in the constructor _RainbowTestState @0xb08fe0-0xb09218.
parser.ignored_events: Frames whose byte[2] != 0x02 are dropped by the b.ne at 0xacfab0 (no throw, no state change). This includes the device's own D2 acknowledgement echo (A5 05 D2 01 7D / A5 05 D2 00 7C, byte[2]=0xD2). No explicit 'skip the first notification' counter exists in this page: filtering is purely by opcode. Additionally, the page closure @0xacf9dc prints the raw frame with dart:core print @0xacfa34 whenever an unresolved no-argument List getter does not equal 185 (0xB9, cmp w0,#0x172 @0xacfa28); that print does NOT suppress parsing (analysisData is called unconditionally @0xacfa48).
parser.error_behavior: No inbound checksum validation was found anywhere in this path (BluetoothModel::getCheckSum @0x80fbbc exists but is not called from write @0x80dd28 nor from testModeSwitch @0xabaef4, and the notification path only forwards bytes). A frame shorter than 7 bytes would raise a RangeError from the sublist/range accesses rather than being rejected gracefully; a wrong opcode returns silently. On the outbound side, BluetoothModel::write @0x80dd28 raises NullCastError if the write characteristic (field_23) or the readiness future (field_3f) is null.

press_release: Every notification carries the ABSOLUTE 32-bit key mask, so there is no separate press or release opcode. analysisData recomputes all mask booleans on every frame: each key k is 'pressed' when (mask & Smi(2^k)) == Smi(2^k) (and x2,x1,x3 + cmp x2,x3 @0xacfc0c-0xacfc18) and 'released' when the bit is clear; results are written to the state's per-key boolean fields listed above. The UI therefore updates on mask transitions only; release is inferred from the bit disappearing in a later frame.
key_id_extraction: Extract the u32 big-endian value of notify bytes [3][4][5][6] (sublist(3,7) @0xacfad0/0xacfad8, big-endian load sequence @0xacfb48-0xacfb88). The key id is the BIT INDEX inside that 32-bit word: byte[6] = bits 0-7 = ids 0-7, byte[5] = bits 8-15 = ids 8-15, byte[4] = bits 16-23 = ids 16-23, byte[3] = bits 24-31 = ids 24-31 (bit == id, no +1 offset). The parser's mask table is exactly a list of powers of two: Smi immediates 2,4,16,32,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,16384,32768,131072,262144,524288,1048576,16777216,33554432 stored at state fields 0x117..0x15b (constructor @0xb0912c-0xb091b4) plus Mint constants 0x4000000,0x8000000,0x10000000,0x20000000,0x40000000,0x80000000 at 0x15f..0x177 (Mint values loaded from pool 0x40000000 @0xb0912c region and PP+0x56448 = 0x80000000 @0xb09208) -> after halving the Smis the tested bit indices are 0,1,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,13,14,16,17,18,19,23,24,25,26,27,28,29,30,31. Ids 2,5,12,15,20,21,22 have no mask constant in this page's table.
